title: Event log line
description: schema_version 3 (from F1c): a trusted line of bin/event_log.py also carries the chain: writer {id: the index's event_writer_id, install_id}, seq (the previous chained line's + 1), prev (that line's mac, or a genesis value for the first) and mac (HMAC-SHA256 hex, with the writer key, of the line's canonical JSON without mac). A line of the agents' untrusted stream (bin/event_untrusted.py) is version 3 with "trusted": false and a source, and has no chain fields. schema_version 2 (from F1b): every line has global_id and install_id. schema_version 1: a line from before the ids. Lines of versions 1 and 2 are never rewritten; they are read and validated as they are, and `event_log.py verify` reports them as legacy, never as proof. The schema subset has no conditional, so the schema accepts every version with the ids and the chain optional; which fields a version has is the writers' rule.

global_id.description: This line's UUID (lower case, version 4), unique: the writer refuses a line whose global_id is already in the log.

install_id.description: The UUID of the install that wrote the line.

auth.description: The owner-auth provider ids whose proofs allowed the change (an apply or rollback of an owner-only row, F1c W4b).

writer.description: The trusted writer that chained this line: its id (index event_writer_id) and its install's id.

install_id.description: The UUID of the writer's install.

seq.description: The chained line's number: the previous chained line's + 1 (the first is 1).

prev.description: The mac of the previous chained line, or the genesis value for the first.

mac.description: HMAC-SHA256 (lower-case hex) with the writer key of the line's canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces, ASCII) without mac.

trusted.description: Only on a line of the untrusted stream: written by anyone, never proof.

source.description: Only on a line of the untrusted stream: who wrote it, as the caller says.
